correctness.rationale: At fixed finite N, the normalized count weights of either stratum are 1+O(ρ) at zero and proportional to ρ binom(N,i)(i−1)! λ^(i−1) at each positive count i. The two-stratum posterior therefore gives the stated pooled rate with z_i=cθ^(i−1). Consecutive subtraction gives a positive factor times (1−θ)i−1−z_i. This bracket is strictly increasing as a function of the real index, and the real crossing obtained with W_0 has the indicated large-c expansion. Strict inequality and the observable endpoint i=N−1 give N_min, including an integer root that does not count. Centering the finite-difference expression at i=m+2 costs only O(1) uniformly, since |j−1|F(θ^(j−φ)) is bounded at both tails. The adjacent-profile difference has the sign of z−1, selecting j=1 for the leading term (a leading-order tie is possible). The size hypothesis includes that index. Varying φ along unbounded sequences realizes the full interval between F(θ)=F(1) and F(√θ). The result is an ordered-limit property of an observational increment; it is not an approximation uniform at positive import, and the statistic is not a physical rate increment. The finite checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: This gives a quantitative diagnostic for an observational artifact: an apparent nonlinear increment can exceed both true component slopes, not merely one, and the discrepancy has no fixed bound in the prescribed sequence of pooled statistics. The exact observable-count threshold and nonconstant modulation are useful for separating pooling selection from a change in the underlying slopes. This is not a result about increasing physical transmission or about a finite-import population.
